result.notes: Burpees at a steady pace to leave 10-15 s of rest; squats unbroken. Breathing is the limiter, so keep moving.
Keep burpees steady so you start each minute with a few seconds in hand; bear crawl fast but low and controlled.

Each station takes about 36-42 s, so you get a short breather before the next minute starts. Stay tall, brace your trunk on the ski erg and drive with the hips, and keep the pace steady so every round looks the same.
Each station should take about 40 s, so hold a steady pace you can repeat and keep the rest of the minute as a short breather. Brace your trunk and keep your ribs down on every Ski Erg pull.
Keep moving at a steady pace: break pull-ups and toes-to-bar into small sets early, before failure forces it.
Hold a steady, sustainable pace on the row and never stand still. Break pull-ups and toes-to-bar into small sets early, before your grip fails.
Round takes about 3:15. Hold a steady pace on the lunges and push-ups so the devil presses stay moving.
Heavy, grindy pace: swings in two sets, take your breaks during the lunges and keep burpees steady. Aim for about 4 minutes per round.
Clean the bar to the front rack once per round and lunge in two sets of 8. Break the pull-ups early to stay ahead of the burpees.
Deadlifts in two sets of 5 with short breaks. Keep lunges steady and the pull-ups in 2–3 sets so grip and legs last all six rounds.
Steady, grinding pace: hold the same round time for 45 minutes. Break deadlifts and pull-ups early rather than failing late, and use the row and run to recover.
Round is about 4:30. Hold a steady pace on the row and run, and keep the deadlifts as quick singles-to-doubles, not a grind to failure. Break the pull-ups early.
Move steadily on the burpees and keep your breathing under control; the deadlifts should be quick touch-and-go sets of 10 and the lunges unbroken if you can.
Move steadily from the first round and keep the burpees non-stop. Your breathing will fail before your legs do, so don't sprint the early rounds.
Grindy pace: pull-ups in one or two sets, rest on the bell rather than the bar. Cleans stop at the shoulder, nothing goes overhead.
Round takes about 2 minutes. Break the pull-ups into two sets early, keep the deadlifts steady, and settle into a rhythm on the burpees.
Steady pace, keep moving through the full window.
Steady pace, never stand still. Run 200 m in about 60 s, then move straight into sit-ups and keep burpees smooth. Work takes roughly 1:45, leaving a few seconds of buffer before the rest.
One pass per interval takes about 1:45: roughly 45 s run, 27 s sit-ups, 20 s burpees, plus transitions. Hold a steady pace and keep moving; use the spare 15 s to reset.
Swings unbroken, snatches in two sets, and keep the burpees steady so your breathing never fully redlines. Hold a pace you can repeat for 16 minutes.
Swings unbroken, fast hinge. Breathing is the limiter, so keep the devil presses steady and move through the burpees without stopping. Expect about 3 minutes per round.
Round takes about 80 s. Move steadily and keep breathing, don't sprint the burpees. Drive the hips hard on every broad jump.
Round is about 1:15. Move steadily on the burpees and keep the broad jumps long and driven from the hips. Breathing will be the limiter, so don't sprint round one.
Reverse lunges and broad jumps hammer glutes and hamstrings. Take slow, controlled lunges and reset before each jump. Keep the double-unders in two sets at most.
Each round is about 2 minutes. Hold the double-unders in one or two sets and slow the lunges down with a pause at the bottom. Break the burpees early, before your legs go.
Keep the thrusters in two quick sets and move steadily through the burpees. Breathing is the limiter, so pace the sit-ups and never redline early.
Keep the thrusters in 2 sets at most and move steadily through the burpees. Your breathing will limit you, so don't redline in the first 3 rounds.
Keep swings unbroken and move fast on the burpees. Break the pull-ups early into 2 sets to hold a steady pace.
Keep every round moving at a steady sprint; swing unbroken, split the pull-ups into two sets early, and keep burpee transitions quick.
Hold a steady pace you could sustain for the full 25 minutes. Keep the thrusters in 2 sets and move through the burpee box jump-overs without stopping.
Keep the dumbbells light enough to move fast and settle into a steady breathing rhythm. Break the thrusters before your lungs force you to, and step over the box if you need to.
Row about 200 m in 50-55 s. Hold the deadlifts unbroken, keep your back flat, and break the wall balls early. A round should take about 3:30-4:00.
Hold a steady pace you could sustain for the full 30 minutes. Hinge with a flat back on the deadlifts and break the push-ups early.
Get-ups are 3 per side, slow and steady. Keep the squats and swings in big, nearly unbroken sets. Your trunk will tire first.
Get-ups are the anchor: steady and controlled, not rushed. Swings and squats go unbroken; the trunk fatigue from the get-ups will bite.
Grip is the limiter: hold the carry and keep the snatches and cleans in big, steady sets. Break early rather than dropping the bag or bell.
Hold steady unbroken sets on the snatches and cleans; the farmers carry will cook your grip, so shake out on the sit-ups. Aim for about 3 minutes per round.
Keep moving at a steady pace: swings unbroken, short breaks on the squats, and settle into a rhythm on the burpees.
Steady pace, never stand still. Swings unbroken, and settle into a rhythm on the burpees early.
Aim for 10 unbroken push presses every round. The bar-facing burpees are where the clock gets away, so move steadily through them.
Aim to hold each set unbroken and keep the bar moving. Your shoulders will fade by round 3, so take short, planned breaks on the push press.
Toes-to-bar is the core slot: go in big sets of 8 or more and break early before the grip fades. Keep the carry tall and steady.
Toes-to-bar is the big slot: aim for 1-2 sets each round. Keep the carry unbroken and hold a steady row pace so the thrusters stay smooth.
Swings unbroken and deadlifts in two sets at most. Run the first rounds controlled so your hamstrings and grip last.
Swings and deadlifts in one or two sets each, with short breaks only before your hamstrings and grip fade. Settle your breathing on the run, then break the burpees early.
Move fast and break pull-ups early into small sets. Hold a steady row pace so the pulling and grip hold up in the later rounds.
Row hard but not all-out. Break the burpee pull-ups early and often, and keep the ring rows and cleans in quick, small sets so the turnover stays high.
Take the double-unders in big sets of 25 or more; stay smooth on the broad jumps and let the burpees be steady, not fast.
Hold steady sets on the sit-ups and rope; stick each broad jump landing with a tall hip hinge to keep the hamstrings and glutes working.
Row hard but keep the stroke rate steady. Break the wall balls into two sets and move to burpees without standing around.
Drive hard with the legs and hips on every row stroke, then go straight to the wall ball. Keep the wall balls to two quick sets and move through the burpees at a steady pace.
Odd minutes swings, even minutes burpees. Each minute should take about 35-45 s; keep moving steadily and use the leftover seconds to breathe, not to stop.
Odd minutes swings, even minutes burpees. Each minute should take about 35-45 s; stay moving and keep the pace steady from the first round to the last.

Minute 1 deadlifts, minute 2 dumbbell snatches (5 per arm), minute 3 burpees. Keep a steady rhythm and aim to finish each minute with 15 s to spare. Grip fades fast, so release the bar and bell between sets rather than clinging.

Minute 1 deadlifts, minute 2 snatches (alternate arms every 5), minute 3 burpees, then repeat. Keep moving steadily; grip will fade, so hold the bar and dumbbell with a relaxed hook and don't redo sets.

Row is the pull and the lung-burner: 10 cal should take about 45 s, so hold a steady pace and don't sprint it. Burpees are the minute that will bite, so move early and finish with a few seconds spare.
Row hard and breathe on the burpees; snatches stay unbroken.
Minute 1 swings unbroken; deadlifts touch and go. Row at a hard sprint, aiming to finish by 40 s. Burpee pull-ups are the pacing trap, so move steadily from the start.
Sprint pace, hinge-heavy: swings unbroken, deadlifts touch-and-go, and aim to leave 10-15 s each minute.
Sit-ups are the big core slot: 16 slow, controlled reps with a pause at the bottom, in two sets of 8. Run the 150 m hard, then use the leftover seconds to breathe before the burpees.
Run 200 m hard but repeatable so you finish with 10+ s to spare. Sit-ups are the big slot: slow, full range, break once if needed. Burpees stay steady to keep the trunk working.
Dumbbell Snatch: alternate arms every rep.
Odd minutes swings, even minutes snatches (alternate arms each rep or switch halfway). Move fast and aim to finish in ~35 s so you can shake out your grip before the next minute.
Odd minutes swings, even minutes snatches (alternate arms each rep). Fast, unbroken sets so you earn 10-15 s of rest; grip will fade, so drop the bell early rather than fight for extra reps.
Clean the bar from the floor to the front rack once, then keep the front squats unbroken. Bike hard for 7 cal (about 42 s) and use the remaining seconds to breathe before the air squats.
Thrusters in one or two sets, cleaning the bar from the floor each minute. Push the bike hard for 7 cal, then take your rest. Air squats should be one smooth unbroken set.
Sit-ups are the core slot. Break swings and squats early into sets of 8-10.

Break pull-ups early into sets of 5-6 and keep rests short. The snatches and deadlifts are heavy, so use small sets and save your grip for the bar work.
Pull-ups, toes-to-bar and chin-ups are the grind: break them early into small sets of 4-6 to keep your grip alive. Move steadily through the dumbbell work.
Hold a pace on the rower you can breathe through, then break wall balls and cleans early into small sets. Keep moving through the burpees.
Row at a pace you could hold for 30 minutes, and break wall balls and deadlifts into sets of 10-15 before your breathing spikes. Burpees are where the workout is won or lost.
Row steady at a pace you could hold for 10 more minutes, then pace the burpee box jump-overs so your breathing stays under control. Break pull-ups early into small sets.
Row at a steady pace you could hold for 10 minutes, since the lungs decide this one. Break pull-ups early in sets of 8-10, and settle your breathing before the burpee box jump-overs.
Hinge-heavy: take steady sets of 15–20 on the swings and deadlifts, and keep your grip fresh for the pull-ups and snatches. Break the burpees early.
Run the first 1600 m easy. Take swings and deadlifts in planned sets of 15-25 with short breaks. Grip and hamstrings will fade, so keep the pull-ups in small, quick sets.
Break the GHD sit-ups into sets of 10 early and keep moving; never sit down between movements.
Keep moving the whole way: break the GHD sit-ups into sets of 10 early, and take any rest during the carry rather than standing still.
Rest 1 min between rounds.

One pass through all three movements per interval, finishing with about 15 s to spare. Go unbroken on the swings, move steadily through the burpees, and keep the deadlifts crisp when your grip and hamstrings are tired.
Do one pass through the list each interval at a sprint pace, then rest for whatever is left of the 2 minutes. Swings unbroken; keep the burpees moving so the deadlifts don't stall.
Rest 1 min between intervals; move fast and unbroken where possible.
Do one round per interval, finishing in about 2:45 and resting in the time left. Pull hard on the row, go in quick sets of 6 on the thrusters, and break the burpees early rather than late.

Each interval is two rounds of the list, about 1:50 per round, finishing with a few seconds to spare. Row hard, do the push press in one or two quick sets, and keep the burpees moving. Start the next round straight away.
Same work every interval; rest the full minute between rounds.

Do 2 rounds in each work window, finishing around 4:45. Pull hard on the ski, hinge fast on the deadlifts, and keep the burpees steady so you don't redline early. Aim for the same pace in all four intervals.

One round per interval, alternating arms on the snatches. Pull hard with the hips on every ski pull and snatch. Keep the ski pace sustainable so you can keep moving through the burpees. Rest in whatever is left of the 3 minutes, about 15-30 s.
Steady pace, keep moving through the whole window and rest only in the final minute.

Hold a steady, conversational-plus pace and keep moving through the whole 4 minutes. Each round takes about 1:55-2:05, so expect two rounds per interval. Break the pull-ups early to protect your grip and keep your legs turning over.

Each interval is a repeating round done for the full 4 minutes (about 1:50 per round, so 2 rounds plus a bit of extra work). Keep a steady pace and never stop moving; break the pull-ups early into 3+3 and count rounds, using any leftover time for extra air squats.
Rest 1 min between intervals.

Rounds of the three movements repeat for the full 3 minutes, aiming for about 3 rounds per interval (the bike takes ~1 min). Sprint the bike, then break wall balls early into 6s and keep the squats fast.
Repeat the round for the full 3 minutes (about 1:30 per round, so two rounds plus a few seconds). Sprint the bike, keep wall balls unbroken, and move fast through the squats.
